title: GPU locality sensitivity and tiling notes — Q2 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to capture operational sensitivity of workload placement/locality and the tiling strategy (interleaving GPU pools across regions) for NA / EU / APAC in advance of the Q2 rollout windows. Not a finalized plan — this is an ops-facing sketch for SRE + capacity + scheduling to iterate on.

Executive summary:
- We observe non-linear latency/cost impact when moving short-lived chat bursts across region boundaries vs colocated serving. This file captures simple heuristics and a small scenario table to guide warm-pool sizing and tiling rules for Q2–Q3 2026.
- Primary ask: define minimum warm-pool per region to preserve 99p latency SLO while enabling opportunistic inter-region burst tiling during sustained low utilization nights.

High-level assumptions (baseline):
- Typical production mix: 65% hosted API low-latency chat, 25% batch embedding, 10% large-batch fine-tune / offline.
- Avg tokens/sec per GPU under gen workloads: 120 tokens/sec (quantized fp16 kernels, trimmed kv).
- Target 99p tail for hosted chat: <= 1400ms for single-turn requests.
- Cold-start penalty for cross-region scheduling (VPN + routing + cache miss) — median +600ms, tail +1.2s.
- Warm-pool recovery time (spin-up + model load + kv restore) for reserved-style machines: 90s median for current images.

Sensitivity heuristics (operational):
- Locality sensitivity factor (LSF): incremental latency (%) when a request is routed away from data locality. Empirically calibrated: NA 1.0 baseline, EU 1.06, APAC 1.12 for cross-zone non-colocated routing.
- Cost delta for opportunistic cross-region: +8–18% token-cost uplift due to additional egress and increased tail retries.

Scenario table (illustrative — per-region 3-month moving windows):
- Baseline utilization target: 68% steady-state targeted across fleet. Warm-pool targets are computed to preserve SLO for 95% of surge events.

Region | Current active GPUs | Target Q2 add | Warm-pool target (min) | Expected 99p tail (local) | Expected 99p tail (cross-region)
NA     | 1,120               | +120         | 90 GPUs (8%)            | 1.25s                   | 1.9s
EU     | 540                 | +60          | 48 GPUs (9%)            | 1.35s                   | 2.0s
APAC   | 260                 | +40          | 36 GPUs (14%)           | 1.5s                    | 2.3s

Notes on table: warm-pool min is conservative vs usual warm-pool because APAC has higher cold-start variance and a smaller margin for egress-based fallbacks. Add numbers reflect committed procurement windows for H2 capacity.

Tiling strategy (operational rules draft):
- Always prefer local serving when local utilization < 85%.
- If local utilization >= 85% and request expected latency budget >= 3s, allow cross-region tiling to NA/EU (prefer nearer region by network RTT). Apply a hard cap of 10% of steady-state RPS for cross-region at any hour.
- During low-utilization windows (00:00–06:00 local), enable opportunistic interleaving: allow workloads from adjacent region within configured cost-sensitivities (set by billing tags).
- Canary policy: enable tiling for 5% sampled requests for 2h, evaluate latency, error, and cost signals to decide scale-up.

Warm-pool choreography and recovery playbook:
- Maintain a minimum sized warm pool per model family (embedding, chat, large-gen). Warm pool inventories updated daily by capacity-scheduler job.
- If warm pool < min for 2 consecutive checks (5m cadence), trigger preemptive spin-up workflow (infra-job: spin-up transient nodes with preloaded weights).
- Forced decommission: drains should be scheduled over 6h windows with warm-pool buffer maintained at +15% to avoid SLO breaches.

Risk matrix (top 6):
1) Model load times higher than expected on new GPU types -> mitigations: staggered rollout, preload kernel cache, synthetic load tests.
2) Network egress cost spike from cross-region fallback -> mitigations: billing throttles, set emergency no-fallback policy flag.
3) Warm-pool erosion during rapid growth -> mitigations: autoscale triggers based on request rate derivative, short spin-up prescaling.
4) Cold-start tail due to KV cache misses after migration -> mitigations: prefix caching, lightweight checkpoint restore.
5) Incorrect tiling heuristics causing capacity hot-spot -> mitigations: telemetry alerting on per-AZ hotspot, automatic route revert.
6) Regulatory/data residency constraints -> mitigations: tagging and hard-route enforcement per customer.

Operational checklists (short):
- Pre-rollout (2 weeks prior): verify region images, run end-to-end synthetic SLO tests, lock warm-pool target config in infra repo (PR + review).
- Day-of-rollout: enable canary tiling for low-traffic cohorts, monitor 1m/5m SLO, monitor egress billing stream, have rollback runbook ready.
- Post-rollout (48h): run capacity backfill simulation, reconcile warm-pool drift, run incident war-room if 99p increased > 15%.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Approve APAC warm-pool at 14% vs conservative 10% tradeoff (finance will push to reduce). Decision required by 2026-03-10.
- Confirm allowed cross-region egress cost budget (suggest cap $35K/month for opportunistic tiling during Q2 pilot).

Action items (owners):
- Aisha P: finalize warm-pool targets and publish to infra-config repo (deadline 2026-03-05).
- Lucas C: run 72h synthetic canary with cross-region tiling at 5% sampling (start 2026-03-02).
- Maya T: add telemetry dashboards for LSF (locality sensitivity factor) and per-request egress bytes (deadline 2026-03-04).
- Ravi S: update autoscale triggers to include request-rate derivative checks (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412).

Appendix — quick math (back-of-envelope):
- Example short-burst demand spike: +18% RPS sustained for 10 minutes in NA. With warm-pool = 90 GPUs and avg capacity 120 tokens/sec, expected servable additional capacity without tiling = ~90 * 120 = 10,800 token/s (approx 18% buffer over baseline). If warm-pool lower by 30 GPUs, cold fallback leads to median latency +350ms and 99p degradation > 20%.

References and links:
- Confluence: "tiling-and-locality-sensitivity" (linked above)
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-9842 (tiling-canary)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 (autoscale triggers)

Notes-to-self: retain simpler conservative defaults for first 8 weeks of pilot. Expect iteration after real traffic canaries.
